sanskrit: tasmin hate rākṣasasainyapāle plavaṃgamānām ṛṣabheṇa yuddhe bhīmāyudhaṃ sāgaratulyavegaṃ pradudruve rākṣasarājasainyam
english: When that guardian of the rākṣasa army had been slain in battle by the foremost of the leaping monkeys, the army of the rākṣasa king, bearing terrible weapons and moving with the speed of the ocean, fled in panic.

sanskrit: gatvā tu rakṣo'dhipateḥ śaśaṃsuḥ senāpatiṃ pāvakasūnuśastam tac cāpi teṣāṃ vacanaṃ niśamya rakṣo'dhipaḥ krodhavaśaṃ jagāma
english: Going to the lord of rākṣasas, they reported that the general had been struck down by the son of Pāvaka; and upon hearing those words of theirs, the lord of rākṣasas fell under the sway of rage.

sanskrit: saṃkhye prahastaṃ nihataṃ niśamya śokārditaḥ krodhaparītacetāḥ uvāca tān nairṛtayodhamukhyān indro yathā cāmarayodhamukhyān
english: Having learned that Prahastha had been slain in battle, tormented by grief and with his mind consumed by anger, he addressed those foremost warriors of the rākṣasas even as Indra addresses the foremost warriors of the immortals.

sanskrit: nāvajñā ripave kāryā yair indrabalasūdanaḥ sūditaḥ sainyapālo me sānuyātraḥ sakuñjaraḥ
english: "No contempt is to be shown toward the enemy, by whom my general — the destroyer of Indra's host — has been slain along with his retinue and his elephants.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ ripuvināśāya vijayāyāvicārayan svayam eva gamiṣyāmi raṇaśīrṣaṃ tad adbhutam
english: I myself, without deliberation, shall go to that wondrous forefront of battle for the destruction of the enemy and for victory.

sanskrit: adya tad vānarānīkaṃ rāmaṃ ca sahalakṣmaṇam nirdahiṣyāmi bāṇaughair vanaṃ dīptair ivāgnibhiḥ
english: Today I shall burn down that monkey army and Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa with torrents of arrows, as blazing fires burn a forest."

sanskrit: sa evam uktvā jvalanaprakāśaṃ rathaṃ turaṃgottamarājiyuktam prakāśamānaṃ vapuṣā jvalantaṃ samārurohāmararājaśatruḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the enemy of the king of immortals mounted his chariot that blazed like fire, yoked with the finest horses, radiant and blazing with its own splendor.

sanskrit: sa śaṅkhabherīpaṭaha praṇādair āsphoṭitakṣveḍitasiṃhanādaiḥ puṇyaiḥ stavaiś cāpy abhipūjyamānas tadā yayau rākṣasarājamukhyaḥ
english: Honored with the sounds of conches, kettledrums, and war drums, with the snapping of fingers, war-cries, and lion-roars, and with auspicious hymns of praise, the foremost king of rākṣasas then set forth.

sanskrit: sa śailajīmūtanikāśa rūpair māṃsāśanaiḥ pāvakadīptanetraiḥ babhau vṛto rākṣasarājamukhyair bhūtair vṛto rudra ivāmareśaḥ
english: Surrounded by the foremost kings of rākṣasas whose forms resembled mountains and storm-clouds, flesh-eating, with eyes blazing like fire, he shone like Rudra attended by spirits and like the lord of immortals.

sanskrit: tato nagaryāḥ sahasā mahaujā niṣkramya tad vānarasainyam ugram mahārṇavābhrastanitaṃ dadarśa samudyataṃ pādapaśailahastam
english: Then, having sallied forth swiftly from the city in great might, he beheld that terrible monkey army, roaring like the ocean and storm-clouds, standing ready with trees and boulders in hand.

sanskrit: tad rākṣasānīkam atipracaṇḍam ālokya rāmo bhujagendrabāhuḥ vibhīṣaṇaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham uvāca senānugataḥ pṛthuśrīḥ
english: Beholding that most ferocious rākṣasa force, Rāma, whose arms were like serpent-lords, attended by his army and endowed with great glory, spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa, the foremost among those who bear weapons.

sanskrit: nānāpatākādhvajaśastrajuṣṭaṃ prāsāsiśūlāyudhacakrajuṣṭam sainyaṃ nagendropamanāgajuṣṭaṃ kasyedam akṣobhyam abhīrujuṣṭam
english: "Whose is this army, unshakeable and fearless, adorned with many banners and standards and weapons, equipped with spears, swords, tridents, missiles, and discuses, furnished with elephants resembling lordly mountains?"

sanskrit: tatas tu rāmasya niśamya vākyaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ śakrasamānavīryaḥ śaśaṃsa rāmasya balapravekaṃ mahātmanāṃ rākṣasapuṃgavānām
english: Then, having heard Rāma's words, Vibhīṣaṇa, equal in valor to Śakra, described to Rāma the foremost champions among those great-souled rākṣasa bulls.

sanskrit: yo 'sau gajaskandhagato mahātmā navoditārkopamatāmravaktraḥ prakampayan nāgaśiro 'bhyupaiti hy akampanaṃ tv enam avehi rājan
english: "That great-souled one seated on an elephant's shoulder, whose face is copper-red like the newly risen sun, causing the elephant's head to tremble as he approaches — know him, O king, as Akampana.

sanskrit: yo 'sau rathastho mṛgarājaketur dhūnvan dhanuḥ śakradhanuḥprakāśam karīva bhāty ugravivṛttadaṃṣṭraḥ sa indrajin nāma varapradhānaḥ
english: That one standing in his chariot with a lion as his emblem, brandishing a bow bright as Śakra's bow, who gleams like an elephant with fiercely bared tusks — he is the foremost of the great ones named Indrajit.

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa vindhyāstamahendrakalpo dhanvī rathastho 'tiratho 'tivīryaḥ visphārayaṃś cāpam atulyamānaṃ nāmnātikāyo 'tivivṛddhakāyaḥ
english: And this one, comparable to Vindhya, Asta, and Mahendra, a bowman standing in his chariot, a surpassing chariot-fighter of surpassing valor, drawing his matchless bow — by name Atikāya, of exceedingly large body.

sanskrit: yo 'sau navārkoditatāmracakṣur āruhya ghaṇṭāninadapraṇādam gajaṃ kharaṃ garjati vai mahātmā mahodaro nāma sa eṣa vīraḥ
english: That great-souled one with copper-colored eyes like the newly risen sun, mounted on a harsh elephant resounding with the clanging of bells, who roars mightily — that hero is known as Mahodara.

sanskrit: yo 'sau hayaṃ kāñcanacitrabhāṇḍam āruhya saṃdhyābhragiriprakāśam prāsaṃ samudyamya marīcinaddhaṃ piśāca eṣāśanitulyavegaḥ
english: That one mounted on a horse with golden and variegated trappings, gleaming like clouds and mountains at twilight, raising a spear bound with rays of light — this apparition moves with the speed of a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa śūlaṃ niśitaṃ pragṛhya vidyutprabhaṃ kiṃkaravajravegam vṛṣendram āsthāya giriprakāśam āyāti so 'sau triśirā yaśasvī
english: And this illustrious one who comes grasping a sharp trident bright as lightning, swift as the vajra of a servant of death, mounted on a lordly bull gleaming like a mountain — he is Triśirā.

sanskrit: asau ca jīmūtanikāśa rūpaḥ kumbhaḥ pṛthuvyūḍhasujātavakṣāḥ samāhitaḥ pannagarājaketur visphārayan bhāti dhanur vidhūnvan
english: And that one of cloud-like form is Kumbha, with a broad and well-formed chest, collected and steady, with the king of serpents as his emblem, who shines as he draws and brandishes his bow.

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa jāmbūnadavajrajuṣṭaṃ dīptaṃ sadhūmaṃ parighaṃ pragṛhya āyāti rakṣobalaketubhūtaḥ so 'sau nikumbho 'dbhutaghorakarmā
english: And this one who comes bearing a blazing, smoke-trailing iron club adorned with gold and vajra-gems, who stands as the standard of the rākṣasa host — he is Nikumbha, of wondrous and terrible deeds.

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa cāpāsiśaraughajuṣṭaṃ patākinaṃ pāvakadīptarūpam rathaṃ samāsthāya vibhāty udagro narāntako 'sau nagaśṛṅgayodhī
english: And this proud one who stands shining on a banner-flying chariot blazing like fire, furnished with bows, swords, and torrents of arrows — that is Narāntaka, who fights on mountain peaks.

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa nānāvidhaghorarūpair vyāghroṣṭranāgendramṛgendravaktraiḥ bhūtair vṛto bhāti vivṛttanetraiḥ so 'sau surāṇām api darpahantā
english: And this one who shines surrounded by spirits of many terrible forms — with faces of tigers, camels, serpent-lords, and lion-lords — with rolling eyes, he is the very crusher of the pride of the gods.

sanskrit: yatraitad indupratimaṃ vibhātic chattraṃ sitaṃ sūkṣmaśalākam agryam atraiṣa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā bhūtair vṛto rudra ivāvabhāti
english: Where that foremost white umbrella shines, resembling the moon, with fine ribs — there the great-souled lord of rākṣasas shines, surrounded by spirits, like Rudra himself.

sanskrit: asau kirīṭī calakuṇḍalāsyo nāgendravindhyopamabhīmakāyaḥ mahendravaivasvatadarpahantā rakṣo'dhipaḥ sūrya ivāvabhāti
english: That diademed one with swinging earrings on his face, of terrible form comparable to the lord of serpents and to Vindhya, the crusher of the pride of Mahendra and Vaivasvata — the lord of rākṣasas shines like the sun."

sanskrit: pratyuvāca tato rāmo vibhīṣaṇam ariṃdamam aho dīpto mahātejā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: Then Rāma replied to Vibhīṣaṇa, the subduer of foes: "Ah, how blazing and of great splendor is Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas!

sanskrit: āditya iva duṣprekṣyo raśmibhir bhāti rāvaṇaḥ suvyaktaṃ lakṣaye hy asya rūpaṃ tejaḥsamāvṛtam
english: Rāvaṇa blazes, hard to look upon like the sun with its rays. I perceive his form clearly — it is enveloped in splendor.

sanskrit: devadānavavīrāṇāṃ vapur naivaṃvidhaṃ bhavet yādṛśaṃ rākṣasendrasya vapur etat prakāśate
english: The form of the heroes among gods and dānavas could not be like the form of the lord of rākṣasas that shines forth here.

sanskrit: sarve parvatasaṃkāśāḥ sarve parvatayodhinaḥ sarve dīptāyudhadharā yodhaś cāsya mahaujasaḥ
english: All his warriors resemble mountains, all fight like mountains, all bear blazing weapons, and all are of great might.

sanskrit: bhāti rākṣasarājo 'sau pradīptair bhīmavikramaiḥ bhūtaiḥ parivṛtas tīkṣṇair dehavadbhir ivāntakaḥ
english: That king of rākṣasas shines, surrounded by blazing, terribly valiant spirits with embodied forms, like Death himself."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rāmo dhanur ādāya vīryavān lakṣmaṇānucaras tasthau samuddhṛtya śarottamam
english: Having spoken thus, the valiant Rāma, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, took up his bow and stood firm, raising an excellent arrow.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā rakṣāṃsi tāny āha mahābalāni dvāreṣu caryāgṛhagopureṣu sunirvṛtās tiṣṭhata nirviśaṅkāḥ
english: Then that great-souled lord of rākṣasas addressed those mighty rākṣasas: "Stand content and without fear at the gates, the patrol-houses, and the city towers."

sanskrit: visarjayitvā sahasā tatas tān gateṣu rakṣaḥsu yathāniyogam vyadārayad vānarasāgaraughaṃ mahājhaṣaḥ pūrmam ivārṇavaugham
english: Having swiftly dismissed them, and when the rākṣasas had gone to their posts, he split apart the ocean-like tide of monkeys as a great fish splits the full surge of the sea.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā samīkṣya dīpteṣucāpaṃ yudhi rākṣasendram mahat samutpāṭya mahīdharāgraṃ dudrāva rakṣo'dhipatim harīśaḥ
english: Beholding that lord of rākṣasas rushing forward swiftly in battle with blazing arrows and bow, the lord of monkeys uprooted a great mountain peak and charged toward the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tac chailaśṛṅgaṃ bahuvṛkṣasānuṃ pragṛhya cikṣepa niśācarāya tam āpatantaṃ sahasā samīkṣya bibheda bāṇais tapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ
english: Grasping that mountain summit with its many trees and ridges, he hurled it at the night-roaming rākṣasa; but seeing it rushing down, Rāvaṇa quickly split it with arrows fletched with gold.

sanskrit: tasmin pravṛddhottamasānuvṛkṣe śṛṅge vikīrṇe patite pṛthivyām mahāhikalpaṃ śaram antakābhaṃ samādade rākṣasalokanāthaḥ
english: When that peak, with its great ridge-trees, was shattered and fell to the earth, the lord of the world of rākṣasas took up an arrow resembling a great serpent and resembling Death himself.

sanskrit: sa taṃ gṛhītvānilatulyavegaṃ savisphuliṅgajvalanaprakāśam bāṇaṃ mahendrāśanitulyavegaṃ cikṣepa sugrīvavadhāya ruṣṭaḥ
english: Seizing that arrow swift as the wind, blazing with sparks and flames, with a speed matching the thunderbolt of Mahendra, he hurled it in rage for the destruction of Sugrīva.

sanskrit: sa sāyako rāvaṇabāhumuktaḥ śakrāśaniprakhyavapuḥ śitāgraḥ sugrīvam āsādya bibheda vegād guheritā kraucam ivograśaktiḥ
english: That arrow, released from Rāvaṇa's arm, with a form like Śakra's thunderbolt and a sharp tip, reached Sugrīva and pierced him with force, as the fierce javelin hurled by Guha pierces a krauñca bird.

sanskrit: sa sāyakārto viparītacetāḥ kūjan pṛthivyāṃ nipapāta vīraḥ taṃ prekṣya bhūmau patitaṃ visaṃjmaṃ neduḥ prahṛṣṭā yudhi yātudhānāḥ
english: That hero, stricken by the arrow, with his senses overthrown, moaning, fell to the earth; and seeing him fallen senseless on the ground, the yātudhānas rejoiced and shouted in the battle.

sanskrit: tato gavākṣo gavayaḥ sudaṃṣṭras tatharṣabho jyotimukho nalaś ca śailān samudyamya vivṛddhakāyāḥ pradudruvus taṃ prati rākṣasendram
english: Then Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Sudaṃṣṭra, Ṛṣabha, Jyotimukha, and Nala, their bodies grown enormous, lifted up boulders and charged toward that lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prahārān sa cakāra meghān rakṣo'dhipo bāṇagaṇaiḥ śitāgraiḥ tān vānarendrān api bāṇajālair bibheda jāmbūnadacitrapuṅkhaiḥ
english: The lord of rākṣasas made those attacks like clouds of theirs [dissolve] with masses of sharp-tipped arrows, and he also pierced those lords of monkeys with networks of arrows with gold-variegated fletching.

sanskrit: te vānarendrās tridaśāribāṇair bhinnā nipetur bhuvi bhīmarūpāḥ tatas tu tad vānarasainyam ugraṃ pracchādayām āsa sa bāṇajālaiḥ
english: Those lords of monkeys, terrible in form, pierced by the arrows of the foe of the thirty gods, fell to the ground; then he covered that fierce monkey army with nets of arrows.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ patitāgryavīrā nānadyamānā bhayaśalyaviddhāḥ śākhāmṛgā rāvaṇasāyakārtā jagmuḥ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ sma rāmam
english: Those monkeys, being slaughtered, their foremost heroes fallen, crying out, pierced with the dart of fear, tormented by Rāvaṇa's arrows, fled to Rāma as their only refuge and shelter.

sanskrit: tato mahātmā sa dhanur dhanuṣmān ādāya rāmaḥ saharā jagāma taṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ prāñjalir abhyupetya uvāca vākyaṃ paramārthayuktam
english: Then the great-souled Rāma, that archer, taking up his bow with arrows, advanced; and Lakṣmaṇa, approaching with joined palms, spoke words of highest significance.

sanskrit: kāmam āryaḥ suparyāpto vadhāyāsya durātmanaḥ vidhamiṣyāmy ahaṃ nīcam anujānīhi māṃ vibho
english: "Though the noble one is certainly fully capable of slaying this wicked-souled foe, I shall destroy this base creature — grant me leave, O lord."

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahātejā rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ gaccha yatnaparaś cāpi bhava lakṣmaṇa saṃyuge
english: The great-splendored Rāma of true valor said to him: "Go, and be most diligent in the battle, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: rāvaṇo hi mahāvīryo raṇe 'dbhutaparākramaḥ trailokyenāpi saṃkruddho duṣprasahyo na saṃśayaḥ
english: "For Rāvaṇa is of great might, of wondrous valor in battle; even if provoked by the three worlds together, he is difficult to withstand — there is no doubt of this.

sanskrit: tasya cchidrāṇi mārgasva svacchidrāṇi ca gopaya cakṣuṣā dhanuṣā yatnād rakṣātmānaṃ samāhitaḥ
english: Seek out his vulnerabilities and guard your own; with eye and bow alike, carefully and with collected mind, protect yourself."

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā saṃpariṣvajya pūjya ca abhivādya tato rāmaṃ yayau saumitrir āhavam
english: Having heard the words of Rāghava, embracing him with honor and bowing to Rāma, the son of Sumitrā then went to battle.

sanskrit: sa rāvaṇaṃ vāraṇahastabāhur dadarśa dīptodyatabhīmacāpam pracchādayantaṃ śaravṛṣṭijālais tān vānarān bhinnavikīrṇadehān
english: He, whose arms were like an elephant's trunk, beheld Rāvaṇa with his terrible bow raised and blazing, covering those monkeys — their bodies shattered and scattered — with nets of arrow-showers.

sanskrit: tam ālokya mahātejā hanūmān mārutātmajā nivārya śarajālāni pradudrāva sa rāvaṇam
english: Beholding him, the great-splendored Hanūmān, son of the wind-god, warding off nets of arrows, charged toward Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: rathaṃ tasya samāsādya bhujam udyamya dakṣiṇam trāsayan rāvaṇaṃ dhīmān hanūmān vākyam abravīt
english: Having approached his chariot and raising his right arm, the wise Hanūmān, threatening Rāvaṇa, spoke these words:

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvā yakṣāś ca saha rākṣasaiḥ avadhyatvāt tvayā bhagnā vānarebhyas tu te bhayam
english: "Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas together with rākṣasas — these you have defeated by virtue of your boon of invulnerability, but you have fear from monkeys.

sanskrit: eṣa me dakṣiṇo bāhuḥ pañcaśākhaḥ samudyataḥ vidhamiṣyati te dehād bhūtātmānaṃ ciroṣitam
english: This right arm of mine, five-branched, raised on high, shall drive the soul long lodged within your body from its dwelling."

sanskrit: śrutvā hanūmato vākyaṃ rāvaṇo bhīmavikramaḥ saṃraktanayanaḥ krodhād idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having heard Hanūmān's words, Rāvaṇa of terrible valor, with eyes reddened by anger, spoke these words:

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ prahara niḥśaṅkaṃ sthirāṃ kīrtim avāpnuhi tatas tvāṃ jñātivikrāntaṃ nāśayiṣyāmi vānara
english: "Strike quickly and without hesitation — win enduring glory; then I shall destroy you as a hero among your kin, O monkey."

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā vāyusūnur vaco 'bravīt prahṛtaṃ hi mayā pūrvam akṣaṃ smara sutaṃ tava
english: Having heard Rāvaṇa's words, the son of Vāyu spoke in reply: "I have struck before — remember your son Akṣa!"

sanskrit: evam ukto mahātejā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ ājaghānānilasutaṃ talenorasi vīryavān
english: Thus addressed, the great-splendored lord of rākṣasas Rāvaṇa, full of valor, struck the son of the wind-god on the chest with his palm.

sanskrit: sa talābhihatas tena cacāla ca muhur muhuḥ ājaghānābhisaṃkruddhas talenaivāmaradviṣam
english: Struck by that palm blow, he swayed again and again; then, greatly enraged, he struck the enemy of the immortals in return with his very palm.

sanskrit: tatas talenābhihato vānareṇa mahātmanā daśagrīvaḥ samādhūto yathā bhūmicale 'calaḥ
english: Then Daśagrīva, struck by the palm of the great-souled monkey, was shaken like a mountain in an earthquake.

sanskrit: saṃgrāme taṃ tathā dṛṣṭva rāvaṇaṃ talatāḍitam ṛṣayo vānarāḥ siddhā nedur devāḥ sahāsurāḥ
english: Seeing Rāvaṇa struck by that palm blow in battle, the sages, monkeys, siddhas, gods together with asuras, all shouted.

sanskrit: athāśvasya mahātejā rāvaṇo vākyam abravīt sādhu vānaravīryeṇa ślāghanīyo 'si me ripuḥ
english: Then the great-splendored Rāvaṇa, recovering, spoke: "Well done! By your monkey valor you are a praiseworthy foe of mine."

sanskrit: rāvaṇenaivam uktas tu mārutir vākyam abravīt dhig astu mama vīryaṃ tu yat tvaṃ jīvasi rāvaṇa
english: Thus addressed by Rāvaṇa, the son of Māruta replied: "Shame upon my valor, in that you still live, O Rāvaṇa!

sanskrit: sakṛt tu praharedānīṃ durbuddhe kiṃ vikatthase tatas tvāṃ māmako muṣṭir nayiṣyāmi yathākṣayam tato mārutivākyena krodhas tasya tadājvalat
english: "Strike just once now, O foolish one — why do you boast? After that, my fist will bring you to destruction." At the words of the son of Māruta, his anger then blazed up.

sanskrit: saṃraktanayano yatnān muṣṭim udyamya dakṣiṇam pātayām āsa vegena vānarorasi vīryavān hanūmān vakṣasi vyūdhe saṃcacāla hataḥ punaḥ
english: With eyes reddened, straining hard, he raised his right fist and with force brought it down on the monkey's chest; the valiant Hanūmān, struck on his broad chest, again staggered.

sanskrit: vihvalaṃ taṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā hanūmantaṃ mahābalam rathenātirathaḥ śīghraṃ nīlaṃ prati samabhyagāt
english: Seeing the mighty Hanūmān then dazed, that warrior supreme among chariot-fighters quickly turned his chariot toward Nīla.

sanskrit: pannagapratimair bhīmaiḥ paramarmātibhedibhiḥ śarair ādīpayām āsa nīlaṃ haricamūpatim
english: With terrible arrows resembling serpents that pierced vital points in the deepest marrow, he set Nīla, the commander of the monkey host, ablaze.

sanskrit: sa śaraughasamāyasto nīlaḥ kapicamūpatiḥ kareṇaikena śailāgraṃ rakṣo'dhipataye 'sṛjat
english: Afflicted by that flood of arrows, Nīla, commander of the monkey host, hurled the peak of a mountain at the lord of rākṣasas with a single hand.

sanskrit: hanūmān api tejasvī samāśvasto mahāmanāḥ viprekṣamāṇo yuddhepsuḥ saroṣam idam abravīt
english: Hanūmān too, splendid and great-minded, having recovered, looking about and eager for battle, spoke these words in anger:

sanskrit: nīlena saha saṃyuktaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram anyena yudhyamānasya na yuktam abhidhāvanam
english: "It is not proper to rush against Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, who is engaged in fighting with Nīla — to attack one already occupied with another."
